# Draft:Sakarwar Clan

Sakarwar clans (Bhumihars, Rajputs, and Kamsar Pathans).
The Sakarwars claim to be descended from two Brahmin brothers who settled in Zamania from Fatehpur district. The Rajput Sakarwars claim descent from the younger brother, Dham Deo Misr, while the Bhumihar Sakarwars and the Pathan Muslim Sakarwars claim descent from the older brother, Kam Deo Misr.
The two Brahmin brothers named Maharaja Kam Deo Misir and Raja Dham Deo Misir came to Ghazipur district and settled at Sakradih first. Due to the flood hazards one of them shifted from the nucleus-Sakradih to Reotipur and the other went to Maa Kamakhya Dham* near Gahmar. From the first brother there descended went to become Sakarwar Bhumihars and Sakarwar Kamsar Pathans emerged and from the second brother there descended went to become Sakarwar Rajputs of Gahmar came into existence. Thus it is clear that the three clans originally belonged to one Gotra from the same Kula.
Dandi Sewami Sahjanand Saraswati claimed that two brothers named Maharaja Kam Deo Misir and Raja Dham Deo Misir came from the Kanyakubja family of Fatuhabad, Fatehpur district and settled at Sakradih, but after sometimes they shifted from original settlement to Reotipur.
Sakarwar clan is one of the most influential clans of the Ghazi-pur district in middle Ganga Valley (U.P.). They belong to the 'Sankrit Gotra' with Kanyakubja Kula**. The main habitat area of Sakarwar Bhumihars/Rajputs, and Kamsar Pathans can be well marked in the Zamania tahsil into two zones: south central and south-eastern part of the Paragana.
